criteria.quote: "Charmeleon only calms when someone else loses."
criteria.revision: Use the Pokédex wording for a sharper, more defensible hook: "Charmeleon constantly seeks opponents. It calms down only when it wins."

criteria.quote: "A tough fight can excite it into bluish-white flames."
criteria.revision: Add the concrete tail detail when introducing strong foes: "When it encounters a strong foe, it becomes aggressive—and the flame at the tip of its tail flares bluish white."

criteria.quote: "What does its temper do before victory finally calms it?"
criteria.revision: Make the unanswered escalation more specific: "Before a win finally calms it, does a tough fight excite Charmeleon—or can agitation incinerate everything around it?"

criteria.quote: "Winning calms it, but agitation can incinerate its surroundings."
criteria.revision: Do not reveal the answer in scene one. Reorder the story so it moves from seeking opponents, to tough fights and bluish-white flames, to strong foes and aggression, to intense flames incinerating surroundings—then reveal last: "It calms down only when it wins."

criteria.quote: "Winning calms it, but agitation can incinerate its surroundings."
criteria.revision: Separate the two flame reveals so the danger lands as a turn: first, "Tough fights can excite it into bluish-white flames." Then later, "If it becomes agitated during battle, it spouts intense flames, incinerating its surroundings."

criteria.quote: "Charmeleon only calms when someone else loses." / "Winning calms it" / "ONLY A WIN BRINGS CALM"
criteria.revision: Remove the repeated calm claim from the opening and reserve it for the final reveal. Let each earlier scene cover one distinct beat: seeks opponents, tough fights excite it, strong foes make it aggressive, and agitation can incinerate surroundings.

criteria.quote: "Victory is its off switch: tough fights excite it, strong foes make it aggressive, and agitation can incinerate its surroundings."
criteria.revision: Make the final line the direct resolution of the opening promise: "After all that—Charmeleon calms down only when it wins." Put the tough-fight, strong-foe, and incineration details before this reveal rather than summarizing them again.

criteria.quote: "Is it chasing calm, or chasing the next fight?"
criteria.revision: Avoid assigning an unsupported motive. Ask a grounded split instead: "What is more alarming: that Charmeleon constantly seeks opponents, or that only winning calms it down?"
